title: Publish personal F-Droid repository and documentation together through CI
description:
## Approved Distribution Decision
Use a developer-operated F-Droid binary repository alongside the existing GitHub Pages docs, not the default f-droid.org catalogue. The user requires no manual steps between deployments. Normal Google Play API submissions can be automated, but Google explicitly documents states after rejected updates that require sending changes for review through the Console; do not promise zero intervention or add a Play-only route. One-time signing/repository setup is allowed as a prerequisite, not recurring release work.

## Scope
Extend .github/workflows/pages.yml and add minimal distribution/fdroid metadata/config and scripts. Target https://secret-camera.standen.link/fdroid/repo/ while retaining the README landing page and PRIVACY.html. Consume verified stable APKs from the tag-release workflow and generate signed F-Droid indexes with pinned fdroidserver tooling.

## Acceptance Criteria
- After setup, a valid release tag automatically builds/signs/publishes the APK and updates the signed repo plus docs: no manual index regeneration, APK copy, web-console action or required environment approval.
- Keep the F-Droid repository signing key distinct from the APK signer, stable across deployments, private in CI secrets and independently backed up. Never publish the key/config secrets or generate a replacement key on each run.
- One serialized Pages publisher assembles both docs and repository on every deployment. A docs-only main push must preserve/rebuild the repo, and an app release must preserve docs; no conflicting deployers or docs-only overwrite.
- Index metadata selects the latest stable CurrentVersion/CurrentVersionCode correctly, retains the latest three stable APKs initially, includes source/license/app description and verifies APK checksum/signing identity before indexing. No fake source-build recipe is required for this binary repo.
- Provide repo enrollment URL/QR and public fingerprint. Users enroll once; update notification/installation behavior depends on F-Droid/Android client capabilities and must not be called guaranteed silent installation.
- In implementation, verify live docs/index/APK URLs, index trust and a normal install/upgrade with synthetic photos as part of development acceptance. No standalone proof task.
- Document that this is a developer repo, not official catalogue inclusion; recheck current Android developer-verification/install requirements without pretending self-hosting removes every platform constraint.

## Sources
https://f-droid.org/docs/Setup_an_F-Droid_App_Repo/
https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9859654
https://developers.google.com/android-publisher/api-ref/rest/v3/edits/commit

## Authorization
Backlog capture only; do not deploy, configure production secrets or publish an APK until implementation is requested.
acceptance_criteria: Every release publishes a trusted F-Droid index/APK and docs in one noninteractive CI flow; docs-only pushes cannot erase the repo.

comments.author: Project Contributors
comments.text: P1: records the selected zero-recurring-manual-step distribution route, dependent only on releasable APK production. User requested ticket capture only; no separate proof ticket and no implementation dispatch.

title: Build, sign and publish Android APK releases automatically from tags
description:
## Scope
Add .github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/workflows/release.yml plus minimal build/signing helpers. Pull requests receive secret-free checks/builds; protected stable v* tags run checks, generate Android with Expo prebuild, build with a pinned compatible Gradle/Android toolchain, sign and publish an immutable APK/checksums/version metadata to GitHub Releases. No iOS jobs, custom app updater or EAS cloud dependency is required.

## Acceptance Criteria
- After one-time approved signing/CI credential setup, a valid protected release tag is sufficient: no recurring workflow approval, console click, manual build/upload or version-counter step between deployments.
- Recover/verify the existing app-signing identity and highest prior version baseline. Do not confuse a Play upload key with the app-signing key; preserve compatible upgrades and photos. Missing credentials block honestly without printing secrets or suggesting uninstall.
- Tag/version validation, diagnostics, lint/typecheck and the project's focused tests run before publication. Use production signing only in trusted tag jobs; do not release Expo template/debug-signed APKs.
- Verify APK signature/certificate, package ID, version and SHA-256 checksum. Store signing material in protected secrets with offline backup instructions; ordinary PRs cannot read it.
- Create GitHub Release assets with explicit stable/prerelease status. Reruns verify/reuse identical published assets and fail instead of replacing a same-version different APK.
- Expose a reliable handoff for the F-Droid/Pages publisher. Invoke it explicitly when added; do not assume a GITHUB_TOKEN-created release event triggers another workflow.
- Include an actual tagged build and downloaded-asset verification as normal implementation acceptance, not a separate proof ticket.

## Authorization
Backlog capture only; no build, release publication or credential changes are authorized by ticket creation.
acceptance_criteria: A valid tag produces a verified signed APK and immutable GitHub Release assets without routine manual steps, using the checked-in deterministic version.

comments.author: Project Contributors
comments.text: P1: the requested primary automated release entry point. User requested ticket capture only; no separate proof ticket and no implementation dispatch.

title: Make Android release versioning deterministic and checked in
description:
## Context
app.json currently reports 1.1.1/versionCode 1, package.json reports 1.0.0, and eas.json uses remote version sourcing with production autoIncrement. The checked-in code therefore does not establish the highest versionCode ever distributed.

## Scope
Make app.json the single checked-in version authority, synchronize package.json/package-lock.json version metadata, and remove the competing EAS remote auto-increment path (use local sourcing if EAS remains). Add a small release/tag validator and concise contributor instructions; no custom release framework.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Establish the real highest previously distributed Android versionCode from existing signed APK/EAS/Play records; do not guess from the stale app.json value.
- A stable vX.Y.Z tag must match the checked-in application version and a positive integer Android versionCode above the previous distributed version. Reject mismatches, duplicate/reused codes and prereleases accidentally targeting stable.
- Building the same tagged commit reads the same versionName/versionCode without an EAS counter or editing generated native files. Reproducible version metadata is required; byte-identical APK reproducibility is not implied.
- Preserve link.standen.secretcamera and provide actionable validation failures before publishing. Tests for one valid tag and representative invalid metadata belong in this task.

## Authorization
Backlog capture only; do not start implementation until requested.
acceptance_criteria: Release metadata comes from one committed authority and the tag validator prevents mismatched or non-increasing Android versions.

comments.author: Project Contributors
comments.text: P1: prerequisite for trustworthy automated releases and in-place upgrades. User requested ticket capture only; no separate proof ticket and no implementation dispatch.

title: Encrypt private photos at rest and automatically decrypt for viewing and sharing
description:
## Scope
Replace the plaintext copy behavior in app/utils/security.ts with authenticated encryption using maintained platform/library primitives and an Android Keystore-backed key strategy. Include app/components/CameraView.tsx, GalleryView.tsx and ImageView.tsx, storage helpers, cache/backup rules and user-facing security wording as needed. Preserve the current private photo directory or migrate it safely.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New stored photos (including persistent thumbnails, if any) are encrypted at rest; plaintext capture/decode intermediates are kept minimal, private and cleaned up. No custom cryptography or hardcoded/exported secrets.
- Existing plaintext photos migrate crash-safely and idempotently: verify durable readable ciphertext before deleting originals; failed/interrupted migration must not lose photos.
- After normal successful app authentication, gallery thumbnails and full-size viewing work automatically without a manual decrypt action.
- Share automatically decrypts only the selected photo to a temporary app-private export and sends a conventional JPEG/image through the existing Android share sheet with narrowly scoped URI read access. The recipient needs neither Secret Camera nor a password/decryption tool.
- Handle success, cancellation, failure, backgrounding and restart with a bounded cleanup policy; do not delete a shared temporary file before the receiver has had time to consume it. Never put plaintext exports into the public media library automatically.
- Document key loss/biometric-change/uninstall/backup behavior and fail visibly rather than silently replacing a lost key or claiming recovery is possible. No private image bytes, keys or decrypted paths in logs.
- Include focused synthetic-photo encrypt/reopen/view/share and migration checks in this implementation; no standalone proof ticket.

## Authorization
Backlog capture only; do not start implementation until requested.
acceptance_criteria: Encrypted stored photos remain readable in-app after authentication and arrive as ordinary images when shared, with safe migration and temporary plaintext lifecycle handling.

comments.author: Project Contributors
comments.text: P1: implements the requested actual at-rest protection, including transparent sharing rather than an encrypted-file export. User requested ticket capture only; no separate proof ticket and no implementation dispatch.

title: Relock private content when returning from background
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
Authenticate, open a private photo or gallery, background Secret Camera, and return. app/index.tsx currently preserves isAuthenticated until unmount, so private content remains accessible without reauthentication.

## Scope
Update app/index.tsx and the existing app/utils/security.ts authentication boundary. Lock/cover private views when leaving the active state; on return require successful device authentication before restoring access. Coordinate with Android biometric-prompt AppState changes and the existing share sheet so neither creates an authentication loop or cancels legitimate sharing. Camera/gallery must not be exposed through a flash of stale UI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A successful login followed by background/resume requires authentication again; cancellation/failure keeps all private content locked.
- No duplicate/infinite prompts from the authentication dialog's own lifecycle transitions.
- Returning from explicit sharing obeys the relock policy without breaking the receiving app's access to the shared image.
- A focused lifecycle regression check and a real Android background/resume demonstration are included in this ticket's implementation; no separate proof ticket.

## Authorization
Backlog capture only; do not start implementation until requested.
acceptance_criteria: Private content stays covered after background/resume until successful authentication, with no prompt loops; existing capture/gallery/share journeys still work.

comments.author: Project Contributors
comments.text: P1: closes an existing bypass of the private-photo authentication boundary. User requested ticket capture only; no separate proof ticket and no implementation dispatch.

title: Remove unused barcode-scanning native dependencies from Android releases
description:
## Context
The existing lock resolves expo-camera 16.0.14, whose Android build unconditionally includes com.google.mlkit:barcode-scanning:17.2.0 and androidx.camera:camera-mlkit-vision. This app does not scan barcodes. Removing a JS prop or unused import does not remove native dependencies.

## Scope
Upgrade Expo/expo-camera to a supported compatible baseline that offers native scanner disabling. Configure barcodeScannerEnabled: false and, for SDKs using prebuilt Expo modules, force expo-camera to build from source using the SDK-supported package.json autolinking buildFromSource setting. Keep configuration regenerable through Expo prebuild; avoid hand-editing ignored generated Android files. Audit any document/code scanner dependencies introduced by the upgraded SDK as well.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Camera capture, front/back switching and private-photo storage continue to work on Android; existing photos are preserved through any FileSystem API migration.
- The resolved release runtime classpath and packaged release APK no longer include the unused barcode/ML Kit scanning implementations; inspect both rather than relying on a boolean or R8 assumptions.
- Inspect compileOnly/build-time scanner dependencies too. Upstream may retain compile-only references even with the runtime feature disabled; record these explicitly and do not claim a completely scanner-free build graph or official F-Droid compatibility while such dependencies remain. If full graph removal needs a maintained source patch or different camera module, document/implement the smallest justified change within this ticket.
- Lockfile and supported Node/Java/Android settings are updated coherently; typecheck/diagnostics and a real camera smoke check accompany implementation, not a new proof ticket.

## Sources
https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/main/docs/pages/versions/unversioned/sdk/camera.mdx
https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/main/packages/expo-camera/android/build.gradle
https://registry.npmjs.org/expo-camera/-/expo-camera-16.0.14.tgz

## Authorization
Backlog capture only; do not start implementation until requested.
acceptance_criteria: Unused barcode scanner runtime dependencies are absent from the release graph/APK, photography still works, and any residual build-only dependencies are honestly documented.
